title: Rigveda 10.160: To Indra
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.160: To Indra: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.160 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Indra. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 139v-140r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.160.1-2 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 18); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 139v
translation.original_text:
1tī̱vrasyā̱bhiva̍yaso a̱sya pā̍hi sarvara̱thā vi harī̍ i̱ha mu̍ñca | indra̱ mā tvā̱ yaja̍mānāso a̱nye ni rī̍rama̱n tubhya̍m i̱me su̱tāsa̍ḥ ||
2tubhya̍ṁ su̱tās tubhya̍m u̱ sotvā̍sa̱s tvāṁ gira̱ḥ śvātryā̱ ā hva̍yanti | indre̱dam a̱dya sava̍naṁ juṣā̱ṇo viśva̍sya vi̱dvām̐ i̱ha pā̍hi̱ soma̍m ||
translation.text:
1TASTE this strong draught enriched with offered viands: with all thy chariot here unyoke thy Coursers. Let not those other sacrificers stay thee, Indra: these juices shed for thee are ready.
2Thine is the juice effused, thine are the juices yet to be pressed: our resonant songs invite thee. O Indra, pleased to-day with this libation, come, thou who knowest all and drink the Soma.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 139v (OPenn image 139, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.159.5 ‹-abhibhūvarī›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 140r, begins in RV 10.160.3 ‹-praśastam ic cārum asmai›. Verses 10.160.1-2 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.160.3-5 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 18); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 140r
translation.original_text:
3ya u̍śa̱tā mana̍sā̱ soma̍m asmai sarvahṛ̱dā de̱vakā̍maḥ su̱noti̍ | na gā indra̱s tasya̱ parā̍ dadāti praśa̱stam ic cāru̍m asmai kṛṇoti ||
4anu̍spaṣṭo bhavaty e̱ṣo a̍sya̱ yo a̍smai re̱vān na su̱noti̱ soma̍m | nir a̍ra̱tnau ma̱ghavā̱ taṁ da̍dhāti brahma̱dviṣo̍ ha̱nty anā̍nudiṣṭaḥ ||
5a̱śvā̱yanto̍ ga̱vyanto̍ vā̱jaya̍nto̱ havā̍mahe̱ tvopa̍ganta̱vā u̍ | ā̱bhūṣa̍ntas te suma̱tau navā̍yāṁ va̱yam i̍ndra tvā śu̱naṁ hu̍vema ||
translation.text:
3Whoso, devoted to the God, effuses Soma for him with yearning heart and spirit,– Never doth Indra give away his cattle: for him he makes the lovely Soma famous.
4He looks with loving favour on the mortal who, like a rich man, pours for him the Soma. Maghavan in his bended arm supports him: he slays, unasked, the men who hate devotion.
5We call on thee to come to us, desirous of goods and spoil, of cattle, and of horses. For thy new love and favour are we present: let us invoke thee, Indra, as our welfare.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 140r (OPenn image 139, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.160.3 ‹-praśastam ic cārum asmai›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 140v, begins in RV 10.161.3 ‹sahasrākṣeṇa śataśāradena śatāyuṣā haviṣāhārṣam›. Verses 10.160.3-5 end on this page; 10.160.3 begins on fol. 139v.
